preconditions.description: The input string s has length l where 3 ≤ l ≤ 5000, consisting only of lowercase English letters.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in stdin.strip())
preconditions.description: Every character in the input string s is a lowercase English letter.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == str(probability) and abs(float(stdout.strip()) - probability) <= 1e-6 * max(1, abs(probability))
postconditions.description: The output is a string representing the optimal probability of Vasya winning, computed as the fraction of possible k values (0 ≤ k < len(s)) for which Vasya can uniquely determine k by optimally choosing one additional character to reveal after seeing the first character of the shifted string t.

postconditions.expression: probability == sum(1 for k in range(len(s)) if is_winnable(s, k)) / len(s)
postconditions.description: The probability is the ratio of the number of k values for which Vasya can uniquely determine k (is_winnable(s, k)) to the total number of possible k values (len(s)).

postconditions.expression: is_winnable(s, k) == any(all(t1 != t2 for t1 in get_possible_shifts(s, k, first_char, extra_pos) for t2 in get_possible_shifts(s, k, first_char, extra_pos) if t1 != t2) for first_char in s for extra_pos in range(1, len(s)))
postconditions.description: A k is winnable if there exists a first character (first_char) and an extra position (extra_pos) such that, after revealing first_char and the character at extra_pos in the shifted string t, no other cyclic shift of s matches both revealed characters.

postconditions.expression: get_possible_shifts(s, k, first_char, extra_pos) == [t[extra_pos] for t in [s[k:] + s[:k]] if t[0] == first_char]
postconditions.description: get_possible_shifts(s, k, first_char, extra_pos) returns the set of characters at position extra_pos in all cyclic shifts of s that start with first_char.
